title: Why Use Radio?
description: Subscribe to [WebSocket](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455) and [Redis Pub/Sub](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/interact/pubsub/) channels from inside DuckDB SQL. Incoming messages buffer into queryable tables; outgoing messages queue with delivery status — all in one process, with no separate consumer service to operate.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Real-time messaging without leaving SQL. The path from "events arriving on a WebSocket" to "rows you can `JOIN` and `WHERE` against" collapses to a subscribe call plus a `SELECT`.

bulletPoints.label: Listen and drain incrementally
bulletPoints.description: Subscribe to a channel and incoming messages flow into an in-memory buffer exposed as ordinary DuckDB tables. Each row tracks how many times it has been seen, so re-querying drains only what's new.

bulletPoints.label: Queue and broadcast outbound
bulletPoints.description: Hand a message to the extension and it delivers asynchronously, with per-message status visible as a table. Poll for delivery, retry, or audit failures from SQL.

bulletPoints.label: Inspect what's connected
bulletPoints.description: Every active subscription shows up as a row with its endpoint, state, and delivery counters — useful for dashboards and runtime debugging.

bulletPoints.label: Test pipelines without the wire
bulletPoints.description: Inject canned messages straight into a subscription's inbox and exercise downstream SQL exactly as it would behave on the real channel.

sections.title: Supported transports
sections.description: Two transports today; the table-function surface stays identical regardless of protocol.

bulletPoints.label: WebSocket
bulletPoints.description: Standard [RFC 6455](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455) client. `ws://` or `wss://` URLs — fits browser-style real-time feeds, Slack-style event streams, and any custom server-sent API that speaks WS.

bulletPoints.label: Redis Pub/Sub
bulletPoints.description: Subscribe to one or more [Redis channels](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/interact/pubsub/) by passing a Redis URL plus channel name. Fits application data flows that already use Redis as the bus.

bulletPoints.label: Roadmap
bulletPoints.description: Google Pub/Sub, Azure Service Bus, MQTT, and subprocess pipes are planned. Today's transports are WebSocket and Redis Pub/Sub only.

sections.title: Production caveats
sections.description: What to know before pointing this at anything important.

bulletPoints.label: In-memory, process-scoped buffers
bulletPoints.description: Received messages live in-process. When DuckDB exits, subscriptions tear down and unread messages are lost. For at-least-once across restarts, drain to a durable store before processing.

bulletPoints.label: Buffers are size-limited
bulletPoints.description: The receive queue has a fixed capacity — older messages are evicted as new ones arrive. Drain frequently enough to keep up with the inbound rate.

bulletPoints.label: Best-effort outbound delivery
bulletPoints.description: Messages are queued and delivered asynchronously. Per-subscription success/failure counters and per-message status tables expose progress so you can build retry logic in SQL.

bulletPoints.label: Single connection per subscription
bulletPoints.description: Multiple DuckDB connections in the same process don't share subscription state. Open a subscription on the same connection that will drain it.

bulletPoints.label: Experimental status
bulletPoints.description: Function shapes may change. Pin a known-good extension version in production.

useCases.title: Live dashboards in DuckDB
useCases.description: Subscribe to a market-data or activity-event WebSocket and refresh a tile by re-querying on a timer. No separate consumer, no message broker.

useCases.title: SQL-driven event responders
useCases.description: Pull events, run the SQL logic, then publish a response back to a Pub/Sub fanout — all in one query loop.

useCases.title: Ad-hoc traffic inspection
useCases.description: Point at a channel you don't yet understand, drain into a `CREATE TABLE AS`, and `GROUP BY` to discover the message shape. Faster than wiring up a custom consumer.

useCases.title: Pipeline testing
useCases.description: Inject canned messages and exercise downstream SQL exactly as it would behave on the real channel.
